p.title: Journey to the centre of the Earth
p.challenge: Dig from the surface to the centre: put the 6 layers in order

panels.t: Crust: thin rocky skin, about 5 km under oceans
Rigid top of the mantle (crust + this = lithosphere)
Asthenosphere: weak, slowly flowing upper mantle
Rest of the mantle, down to about 2,900 km
Outer core: liquid; S waves cannot pass
Inner core: solid nickel and iron (nife)

p.title: Moving plates and drifting continents
p.challenge: Find the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (divergent), Himalayas (convergent), San Andreas Fault (transform) and both Mesosaurus fossil sites

points.name: Himalayas
points.info: Convergent boundary: plates move towards each other.

points.name: San Andreas Fault
points.info: Transform boundary: plates slide past each other.

points.name: Brazil: Mesosaurus fossils
points.info: Fossils of the same reptile, Mesosaurus, are found in Brazil and South Africa.

points.name: South Africa: Mesosaurus fossils
points.info: These lands were once joined in Gondwanaland.

points.name: India: old glacial tillite
points.info: Tillite in India and other southern lands shows they were once joined. India was part of Gondwanaland.

p.title: Inside an earthquake
p.challenge: Arrange what happens in an earthquake, from stored stress to the seismograph

nodes.text: Energy is stored in rocks along a fault
nodes.info: Faults are usually near plate boundaries.

nodes.text: Rocks suddenly slip at the focus
nodes.info: The focus (hypocentre) is inside the Earth; the epicentre is the point on the surface right above it, where shaking is usually strongest.

nodes.text: Surface waves arrive last and do the most damage
Seismograph record: magnitude on the Richter scale
nodes.info: Intensity (shaking and damage felt) is measured on the Mercalli scale, 1 to 12.

p.title: Active, dormant or extinct?
p.challenge: Think of Barren Island in the Andamans. Answer the questions to find its type

nodes.text: A volcano: an opening (vent) in the crust
nodes.info: Magma is molten rock below the surface; it is called lava once it comes out.
Barren Island in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is India's only active volcano.
Some volcanoes stay quiet for a long time but may still erupt.
Quiet for a long time but may erupt again.

p.title: Rocket ride up through the atmosphere
p.challenge: Order the 5 layers from the ground upwards

panels.t: Troposphere: almost all weather and clouds
Stratosphere: ozone layer; good for aeroplanes
Mesosphere: coldest layer; meteors burn up
Exosphere: the air is extremely thin

p.challenge: x = height in km, y = temperature in °C. At sea level it is 30 °C. Set the slope so it gets 6.5 °C colder for every 1 km you climb
p.winText: Right! Temperature falls about 6.5 °C per 1,000 m, so 2 km up it is about 17 °C. That is why hill stations like Shimla and Ooty are cool.

p.title: Spring tide or neap tide?
p.challenge: It is a full-moon night at the beach. Answer the questions: what kind of tide will you see?

nodes.text: Tides: the sea rises and falls
nodes.info: Caused mainly by the pull of the Moon's gravity, helped by the Sun. Most coasts get two high and two low tides a day.
Spring tides are the highest tides. They come at full moon and new moon.
Neap tides have the smallest rise and fall. They come when the Moon is at its quarters.
